topic: Type Alias with `typedef` and `using` in Modern C++
explanation: In C++, creating type aliases allows programmers to define alternative names for existing types, improving code readability and maintainability. While `typedef` has been traditionally used for this purpose, modern C++ (C++11 and beyond) introduces the `using` keyword as a more versatile and clearer way to define type aliases, especially for complex or template types. This concept is essential for writing clean, expressive, and generic C++ code, particularly when working with STL containers and template programming.
keywords: C++ type alias, typedef vs using, C++ alias declaration, modern C++ type naming
